topic: Bias-corrected weak-signal inference for a growing-window ATT under serially dependent deterministic-MNAR panel completion. Fix exact known rank and dependence range, impose explicit normalized donor/pre restricted-Gram bounds, and let the treated cohort and consecutive post window grow. For Choi--Yuan's subgroup nuclear-norm estimator and rank-projection debiasing, derive the complete donor-window plus treated-pre minus donor-pre tangent score. Transfer neighborhood-noise-replaced auxiliary fits through the actual masked convex optimizer, derive the serial quadratic drift and a feasible Hessian--lag-covariance correction, and bound the corrected signed aggregate remainder at the oracle window standard-error scale on an explicit joint signal/window envelope polynomially weaker than strong-factor order. Prove an independent-row CLT, consistency of an influence-weighted finite-lag residual covariance estimator, and uniform Wald coverage for the realized cohort-window ATT. Credit Choi--Yuan arXiv:2402.05789 for fully observed leave-neighbor-out weak-factor analysis and Cen--Lam arXiv:2403.13153 for missing-factor residual HAC; do not claim event-time bands, unknown rank, or proportional-window inference at the noise boundary. Consumer: the SEC Tick Size Pilot sustained-liquidity-effect reanalysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact proximal identity Mtilde=SVT_lambda(P_Omega Y+P_missing Mtilde), the complete three-term local differential, and the rank-one projection quadratic map. For constant-factor MA(1) panels it derived a serial quadratic coefficient converging to -1/psi and an estimable Hessian--lag-covariance correction; a separate weak-signal block-mean case has exact remainder O_P(1/(n psi)) and oracle variance 36/n^2-64/n^3 versus iid 20/n^2. Hidden-block nonidentification, rank overprojection, window-growth boundaries, covariance degeneracy, residual contamination, and nearby literature were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform native-optimizer second-order transfer and plug-in stability, including centered quadratic aggregation and higher-order/regularization errors o(s), from primitive conditions. EARLY KILL TEST: At rank one with Gaussian MA(1), constant and positive alternating factors, H proportional to n, and psi=n^(4/5), reproduce the three-term derivative and exact quadratic coefficient, apply the fitted correction, and certify that n times the corrected native-optimizer remainder vanishes; a surviving interior term or strong-factor requirement forces pivot. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_mnar_window_blockloo.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior review evidence rejects an analogous estimator-stability rate because no primitive learner class or derivation discharged it. Existing web anchors separately establish auxiliary equivalence for nuclear-norm initialization and neighborhood deletion for fully observed PCA. Under deterministic treatment-block masking, however, replacing a temporal noise neighborhood perturbs the KKT system, active singular spaces, and rank projection globally. The first proof step that must change is therefore a sensitivity expansion of the masked singular-value-thresholding fixed point, uniform across the growing cohort-window; current arguments do not control its centered quadratic, higher-order, and regularization terms at the shrinking ATT standard-error scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A high-probability native-optimizer perturbation theorem giving the complete donor-window plus treated-pre minus donor-pre first derivative and explicit uniform bounds that make the centered quadratic, cubic, and penalty-induced signed aggregate remainders o_P of the oracle ATT standard error.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing distinguishes a proof-only auxiliary fit from the estimator actually implemented, which is precisely the native-optimizer transfer issue.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Using all observed entries improves completion -> estimator-target dependence obstructs inference -> a leave-out proof device must be coupled back to the implemented masked optimizer -> serial neighborhoods and growing aggregation require second-order coupling

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the hypothetical leave-one-out construction and convex-estimator equivalence proof, replacing pointwise first-order control by uniform neighborhood-level second-order control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest existing bridge between an auxiliary leave-out object and an implemented nuclear-norm estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer leave-neighbor-out conditioning and recursive higher-order singular-space perturbation under finite-range dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its deletion geometry matches the serial neighborhoods, although the destination must carry the argument through an implicit masked proximal optimizer.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the convex-to-nonconvex bridge and entrywise perturbation proof for nuclear-norm regularization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The bridge supplies fine control of an actual convex solution, but must be rebuilt for deterministic causal blocks and dependent neighborhood replacement.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior review shows that an oracle-looking variation condition is insufficient without primitive estimator-side rates. Cen–Lam's feasible HAC argument applies to covariance-PCA loading scores under a different missingness mechanism, while existing causal-panel intervals are pointwise or bootstrap based. Here the fitted residuals share native-optimizer error with all three tangent-score blocks, their lag products reuse local noise neighborhoods, and the estimated influence weights also enter the Hessian drift correction. The first missing proof step is a feasible-minus-oracle decomposition into centered serial products, influence-weight error, and masked-optimizer residual contamination, with every component controlled at the shrinking aggregate scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform plug-in consistency theorem for an explicit influence-weighted finite-lag covariance estimator and Hessian-lag correction, followed by a nondegenerate studentized independent-row CLT and uniform Wald coverage for the realized cohort-window ATT.

writing_exemplar.why: Its path from factor-based counterfactual imputation to implementable treatment-effect intervals closely matches the destination's inference last mile.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Panel completion produces counterfactual estimates -> serial dependence invalidates naive uncertainty formulas -> weak-signal growing-window aggregation adds fitted-score contamination -> feasible covariance and drift correction are required for Wald inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior review makes rate attainability under primitive conditions a load-bearing obligation. Increasing cohort and window sizes reduces oracle variance through averaging, but also enlarges the deterministic missing block, degrades observed-data Gram geometry, and accumulates projection curvature, regularization bias, and optimizer-transfer error. Existing papers cover only separate faces of this trade-off: small-group weak-signal MNAR inference, average-effect limits under stronger geometry, or weak-factor-uniform regression designs that exclude the relevant common-start policy block. The first proof step is to derive every signal and window power from the native proximal expansion and serial lag contractions, rather than impose strong-factor order; sharpness then requires a matching rank-one finite-range-dependent failure construction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An upper-and-lower phase theorem giving explicit polynomial signal-cohort-window inequalities under which the corrected signed remainder is o_P of the oracle ATT standard error, plus a rank-one Gaussian finite-range-dependent counterexample identifying the first nonvanishing term outside the envelope.

writing_exemplar.why: Its small-missing-group versus statistical-efficiency trade-off is the natural narrative to sharpen into a three-way signal, cohort, and window frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment creates deterministic block missingness -> subgrouping restores weak-signal inference for small missing sets -> growing aggregates improve oracle precision while worsening completion geometry -> corrected inference needs an explicit joint phase boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt minimax linear-bias control and least-favorable weak-factor comparisons to obtain uniform upper bounds and impossibility statements.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly studies factor-strength-uniform inference and demonstrates when oracle strong-factor behavior cannot be replicated.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the higher-order weak-factor expansion and signal-indexed remainder bookkeeping, adding growing-window accumulation and serial lag contractions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its expansion most directly reveals which inverse-signal powers can become binding at a weak-factor boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt double debiasing and tangent-space projection for a growing-support linear matrix functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cohort-window ATT is a structured linear form whose weight norm and singular-space alignment determine both variance and projection remainder size.

literature_map:
1. Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA, arXiv:2308.02364) give subgroup nuclear-norm completion and debiased weak-signal inference for deterministic MNAR causal blocks, but assume independent noise and leave dependence open.
2. Choi and Yuan (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2402.05789) handle weak factors and dependent noise through leave-neighbor-out analysis, but for fully observed PCA rather than masked convex completion.
3. Cen and Lam (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2403.13153) combine weak factors, missing tensor observations, serial dependence, and residual HAC inference; their target and missingness mechanism differ from the causal block problem.
4. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2307.16370) couple an auxiliary leave-one-out fit to a nuclear-norm initializer, providing the closest native-estimator transfer but not serial second-order control.
5. Xia and Yuan (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:1909.00116) develop double debiasing and tangent projection for general linear matrix functionals under random sampling and independent errors.
6. Su and Wang (2025, Journal of Econometrics, DOI:10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106022) derive average-treatment-effect limits under broad missing patterns, without the weak-signal growing-window nuclear-norm frontier.
7. Xiong and Pelger (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1910.08273) give entrywise factor-imputation inference under general missing patterns and dependent errors, using different factor-strength and estimator geometry.
8. Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2202.12078) establish residual-bootstrap coverage for pointwise panel treatment effects, not analytic growing-window ATT inference.
9. Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026, JPE, arXiv:2210.06639) give weak-factor-uniform bias-aware inference but exclude the common-start subset policy indicator relevant here.
10. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA, arXiv:1710.10251) establish causal panel matrix completion with treatment-induced missingness, primarily at estimation rather than weak-signal serial inference depth.
11. Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen (2023, COLT, arXiv:2109.15154) prove entrywise guarantees for causal MNAR completion through synthetic nearest neighbors, a structurally different estimator.
12. Bai and Ng (2021, JASA, arXiv:1910.06677) and Cahan, Bai, and Ng (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2103.03045) provide foundational block-imputation and residual-overlay results under stronger factor regimes.
13. Ben-Michael and Feller (2026, JASA discussion, arXiv:2602.21314) identify subgroup efficiency choices and the statistical last-mile problem as unresolved practical issues.
14. The unoccupied conjunction is deterministic causal-block missingness, the implemented subgroup convex optimizer, weak singular values, finite-range serial noise, a growing cohort-window ATT, and feasible curvature-corrected Wald inference.
